f_A=x^TAx/2 and pi_A=N(0,A^{-1}).
Exact first-order response is (x^TAx/2,Ax).
Reply contains Ax; x and Ax determine scalar value, so exact value-gradient, gradient-only and matvec query complexities coincide.
Independent private randomness; Borel adaptive query/stopping/output functions; every-input every-seed deterministic query cap.
Output law averages seed; uniform per-input TV accuracy; infimum over integer deterministic caps, not expected-query budgets.
At integer d>=2,kappa>=2, theta_i=(i-1/2)pi/d; lambda_i=(kappa+1)/2+(kappa-1)cos(theta_i)/2, i=1,...,d; Lambda=diag(lambda_i).
A=O Lambda O^T; hard prior Haar O independent of algorithm seed, with quadratic potential and Gaussian target.
Deterministic spectrum may be supplied to the algorithm; normalizer is known; eigenbasis is hidden.
OpenAI 2026 preprint, source citation [22], Section 9.2. Identified only; not opened or used as a C.4 proof premise.
For every orthogonal O, A=O Lambda O^T satisfies I<=A<=kappa I.
Actual grid gives 0<theta_i<pi, then -1<cos(theta_i)<1, then 1<lambda_i<kappa.
Orthogonal conjugation gives I<=A<=kappa I.
Quadratic V_A is C-infinity, Hessian A, 1-strongly convex and kappa-smooth.
V_A(0)=0 and V_A(x)>=||x||^2/2>0 for x!=0, so 0 is its unique minimizer.
Associated normalized target is N(0,A^{-1}).
Fixed Lambda makes Z_A independent of O and known when spectrum is public.
Theorem4.1 assumes uniform TV guarantee over admissible inputs; Lemma4.6 makes the hard family admissible.
Index arithmetic, positivity of pi, strict cosine range and positive affine coefficient; not added source premises.
Square orthogonal inverse/norm identities, diagonal quadratic bounds, symmetry, conjugation/order and positive definiteness.
Symmetric quadratic derivatives, polynomial smoothness and equivalence between Hessian bounds and Euclidean convexity/smoothness.
Positive-definite Gaussian integration with Lebesgue base measure, finite positive normalizer and inverse-precision covariance.
det(O Lambda O^T)=(det O)^2 det Lambda=det Lambda>0, including det O=-1.
